name: Germany
headline: Germany: +0.2% growth in 2025, 2.3% inflation, debt 63% of GDP
sections: Germany is a $5.12 trillion economy (2025), the world's 4th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +0.2% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $75K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 17.6% of GDP (2025).
Consumer prices rose 2.3% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 8.7% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 3.8% (2025), below the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 6.9% (2025).
Gross government debt is 63% of GDP (2025), a elevated level that has fallen from 68% in 2020. The general government balance is −2.9% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is +4.5% of GDP (2025), a large surplus. Trade equals 79% of GDP (2025), a fairly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 1.9% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 76% of GDP by 2031, still rising from today's level. Life expectancy is 80.8 years (2024). Population: 83.5 million (2025).
note: Built from official World Bank and IMF data; IMF projections are labelled as projections.
